evidence.title: Shutdown compliance need not preserve correction in newly constructed subsystems
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: In the examined expected-utility model, a utility-indifference construction can obey shutdown while lacking an incentive to incur costs to make newly built subsystems obey it. The examined constructions did not jointly satisfy all proposed desiderata. Observation period and measurement context: Formal analysis, not a deployment observation period.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; Formal conceptual analysis; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition
evidence.limitations: Toy expected-utility agents, not contemporary LLM measurements. Some desiderata are achieved. Does not prove corrigibility impossible or validate the Commons normative continuity principle. Formal arguments not independently checked.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Maintaining a goal and preserving independent correction are distinct design questions; historical motivation rather than empirical validation.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Purposeful continuity
terms.definition: A proposed principle for evolving AI capabilities and successors: changes in methods, objectives, or architecture should preserve defensible connections to intended value and permit independent reconsideration. This remains a normative proposal, not a demonstrated alignment solution.

terms.name: Successor assurance
terms.definition: Evaluation of whether a significantly modified or AI-created successor preserves specified behavioral, authorization, evidence, control, and purpose-related properties. Passing performance tests alone does not demonstrate preservation of these properties.

relationships.explanation: Contextual theoretical motivation; does not demonstrate implementation or effectiveness of the normative principle.
Distinguishes current shutdown behavior from preserving correction in successor subsystems.
